text: Thirty lessons, one throughline: taking the real-time ingestion ideas Fabric's Eventstreams already introduced and learning the vendor-neutral tool most of the industry actually builds that pattern on.

Chapters 1 through 3 built Kafka's own architecture: a durable log instead of a queue, producers and consumers, replication, retention. Chapters 4 and 5 added Connect, Streams, ksqlDB, and Kafka running in the cloud. Chapters 6 and 7 put it all to work: real pipelines, real integrations with Snowflake and Databricks, security, and this capstone.

This course was the last of four courses in the Azure/Fabric Data Engineer path's Advanced stage. Git/GitHub/CI-CD, Terraform & Bicep, and Airflow were already built — Kafka closes that stage out completely.

That completes both stages: Job Ready's six courses, from T-SQL through Career & Capstone, and now the Advanced stage's four — Git/CI-CD, Terraform/Bicep, Airflow, and this course. Ten courses, one finished path.
That's Kafka & Event Streaming — and with it, the entire Azure/Fabric Data Engineer path. Congratulations on finishing all ten courses.
